supportingEvidence.note: Reports a proposed joint temporary navigational corridor and mine clearing, while also reporting a tanker disabled by an unidentified projectile near Oman the same day.

supportingEvidence.note: Brent fell to about $86.80 and WTI to about $80.87 as markets priced de-escalation/reopening optimism.

supportingEvidence.title: Oman Foreign Ministry: temporary maritime-corridor mechanism for Hormuz
supportingEvidence.note: Primary Omani background confirms an established policy and coordination mechanism for temporary corridor access and freedom of navigation.

contradictingEvidence.title: Reuters: diplomatic progress remains incomplete and passage remains perilous
contradictingEvidence.note: The talks themselves could still produce an operational corridor quickly; one attack may be an isolated event rather than evidence that the broader reopening path is failing.

realityDelta.falsifier: A sustained multi-day rise in independent vessel throughput, declining war-risk/freight premiums, no further maritime attacks, and restored refined-product deliveries make incident-level security data add no predictive value over the public corridor-talk and oil-price baseline.

evidence.title: Reuters reporting on tanker strike near Oman and Hormuz corridor talks

realityDelta.title: Hormuz reopening optimism diverges from physical security after fresh tanker strike
realityDelta.summary: Markets and diplomacy are shifting toward reopening optimism, but a fresh tanker strike near the Strait entrance shows the physical-security state has not normalized. Narrative, price, and incident-level evidence are diverging.
realityDelta.delta: Refine CONTESTED_REOPENING into a two-layer state: diplomatic/market de-escalation is improving, while physical maritime-security confirmation remains incomplete. Do not advance to NORMALIZING until throughput, attack frequency, freight, insurance, and product-delivery data confirm the move.
firstOrderImpacts: continued downside pressure on oil risk premium if talks progress
persistent war-risk and freight uncertainty despite lower crude prices
greater value of incident-level maritime monitoring for validating reopening
secondOrderImpacts: possible divergence between crude-price optimism and shipping/insurance economics
lower energy-inflation expectations could reverse quickly if attacks continue
alternative-data value shifts toward measuring realized physical security rather than summarizing diplomatic statements

alphaHunter.hypothesis: Incident-level maritime security plus independent vessel/freight data will identify failed or fragile reopening states earlier than diplomatic statements and Brent price action alone.
alphaHunter.baseline: Iran-Oman corridor statements plus Brent/WTI reaction
alphaHunter.alternativeData: UKMTO/JMIC incident events, independent vessel throughput, war-risk insurance, tanker freight, and refined-product delivery data
alphaHunter.incrementalValueMetric: 3-7 day forecast error for confirmed throughput/security normalization versus the public diplomatic/price baseline
alphaHunter.killCondition: Kill the extra data layer if it fails to improve held-out reopening-state forecasts or arrives too late to change a research decision.

evidence.title: AP reporting on Hormuz navigation talks

realityDelta.title: Hormuz shifts from pure disruption toward contested reopening
realityDelta.summary: Reported mine-clearing of the main shipping lane and renewed Iran-Oman corridor negotiations reduce immediate navigational risk, but transit remains politically and militarily conditional rather than normalized.
realityDelta.delta: Supersede the binary open/closed model with a state transition: severe disruption -> partially demined / negotiated corridor -> contested reopening. Physical throughput and freight/insurance data must confirm the transition before confidence rises further.
firstOrderImpacts: possible easing in freight and insurance stress
secondOrderImpacts: reduced energy-inflation pressure if physical flows recover
lower tail-risk premium in rates and risk assets
greater value of real-time vessel-flow validation versus political statements

alphaHunter.hypothesis: Independent physical-flow data will confirm or reject the claimed reopening faster and more reliably than official political statements or oil-price reaction alone.
alphaHunter.baseline: Official mine-clearing / corridor statements plus Brent price reaction
alphaHunter.alternativeData: Independent vessel counts/throughput, freight rates, war-risk insurance, and later refined-product delivery data
alphaHunter.incrementalValueMetric: Forecast error for 3-7 day confirmed throughput and freight/insurance normalization versus the baseline
alphaHunter.killCondition: Kill the added complexity if public/low-cost physical-flow data cannot beat the baseline on held-out outcomes or arrives too late to change a decision.

relations.relation: broadens solicitation scope beyond AI-only solutions

supportingEvidence.title: SAM-derived mirror showing Amendment 0002 dated Aug. 24, 2026
supportingEvidence.note: Shows Amendment 0002, broadened scope, and current Aug. 27 FY2026 response deadline.

supportingEvidence.title: Independent SAM-derived mirror of DHS procurement-modernization CSO
supportingEvidence.note: Corroborates scope expansion beyond AI-only solutions and Aug. 27, 1:00 p.m. ET deadline.

contradictingEvidence.title: Stale SAM-derived mirror still showing Aug. 26 deadline and AI-only focus-area framing
contradictingEvidence.note: Useful evidence that procurement intelligence must model notice versions and supersession instead of trusting one cached page.

opportunityRadar.falsifier: Official SAM.gov Amendment 0002 materially differs from these mirrors, or DHS supersedes the Aug. 27 FY2026 deadline/scope again.
opportunityRadar.title: DHS broadens procurement-modernization CSO and moves FY2026 deadline
opportunityRadar.thesis: Version-aware procurement-change detection is a high-value Opportunity Radar primitive because amendments can change eligibility, urgency, and market size after the original notice is published.
opportunityRadar.whyNow: The Aug. 24 amendment materially changes both scope and timing versus the original Aug. 17 notice.

score.veto: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE: economics and fit are not yet defensibly scored

opportunityRadar.recommendedNextAction: Run the amendment through the truthful Wayfinder gating path and compare it against the prior notice version; do not bid or contact DHS.
evidenceRequiredToAdvance: official SAM.gov Amendment 0002 text or direct registry API evidence
